AddFromBenchBody.description:
Add a bench company to today's list. `idempotencyKey` is `bench:<companyId>:add`: once it landed, the same
key answers with the row and writes nothing.
AddFromBenchBody.title: AddFromBenchBody

BenchCompany.description: One company of the bench ("More options"), in the compact shape of a pick row.
BenchCompany.title: BenchCompany

CompanyProfile.description:
What does not change about a company (the Today redesign): what it builds, how big and where, its visa position,
its open roles at his level, the people on record and his own history with it. Every line is the API's.
CompanyProfile.title: CompanyProfile

CompanyQueue.description: A company row's lines (company first, #9 2026-10-26). Every line is the API's; the page shows them as given.
CompanyQueue.title: CompanyQueue

CompanyResumed.description: A resume: how many drafted or approved emails were waiting on the pause, and the new revision.
CompanyResumed.title: CompanyResumed

CompanyWritten.description: The company's new revision, after a pause, close or reopen.
CompanyWritten.title: CompanyWritten

CorrectionBody.description: Set one outcome to `at` (any ISO-8601 time) or clear it (`at` null), from the touch's history.
CorrectionBody.title: CorrectionBody

EmailFitView.description:
Whether a cold email is worth it at this company (`outreach.plan.email_fit`, 2026-10-27): `email` or
`linkedin_only`, with short reasons in plain words, the most important first (every blocker when LinkedIn only).
It only flags the company: he brings the people, Claude drafts, he approves in the Outbox.
EmailFitView.title: EmailFitView

Empty.description: The answer of a write that has nothing to report: JSON `{}`, never an empty body.
Empty.title: Empty

HiddenCompany.description: A company the ranker hides, with the reason it stored. `provisional` is "hidden, pending reader".
HiddenCompany.title: HiddenCompany

HoldingReply.description: The newest reply holding the company: on any channel, so a LinkedIn reply shows as an email one does.
HoldingReply.title: HoldingReply

InFlightCompany.description: A company with a wave out in the last `linkedin.rotate_days`, or a reply: the track half of the queue.
InFlightCompany.title: InFlightCompany

LinkedInActivity.description:
Counts only, no rate: people with a live LinkedIn request (messaged) and people with a live reply step
(replied), over the last 7 New York days (today and the 6 before) and in all. A reply in the window may answer a
request from before it, so the two are never divided.
LinkedInActivity.title: LinkedInActivity

LogAppliedBody.description: He applied to the row's role. `idempotencyKey` is `plan:<entryId>:apply`. `revision` as `LogRequestBody`.
LogAppliedBody.title: LogAppliedBody

LogPeopleBody.description:
The people he asked at a company row, pasted as `Name | Title | note` lines (up to 10; the terminal's paste
block `Company | Name | Title | note` is read too). The API reads the lines; the page sends them as typed.
`idempotencyKey` is the paste's own key (`plan:<entryId>:people:<n>`): line n's touch key is `<key>:<n>`, so the
same paste sent twice writes once.
LogPeopleBody.title: LogPeopleBody

LogRequestBody.description:
He sent the LinkedIn request by hand. `idempotencyKey` is the touch's own key (`plan:<entryId>:request`): one
touch per key, whatever the request id. `revision` is optional and never checked: a log only adds a touch, the key
stops a double press, and two logs sent out of order (the tab closed) must both land. The entry's revision still
moves on.

A row with a person sends its `personId`. A company row (nobody on it: company first, #9) sends `personName`
instead, the name of the person he asked; the person is added at the company (by him) or found there by name.
LogRequestBody.title: LogRequestBody

LogStepBody.description:
A step he took on LinkedIn by hand. `replyKind` goes with `replied` and nothing else; an out-of-office is
not a reply, so `auto_reply` is not a kind here.
LogStepBody.title: LogStepBody

LogTouchBody.description: A touch he made himself: a reply to an HN post, or any other touch. The other channels have their own writes.
LogTouchBody.title: LogTouchBody

LoggedPerson.description: One line of a pasted people log, as written.
LoggedPerson.title: LoggedPerson

MergeCompare.description:
Both sides of a merge question (`outreach.review.merge.merge_compare`): `a` is the item's company, `b` the one
its key names.
MergeCompare.title: MergeCompare

MergeSide.description: One company of a merge question, as `outreach.review.merge.MergeSide` reads it.
MergeSide.title: MergeSide

OutcomeBody.description: An answer to "what came of this?". `quiet` is "Nothing yet": a snooze before day 21, then the quiet mark.
OutcomeBody.title: OutcomeBody

PassPickBody.description:
Not now on a pick. `reason` is one of the chips, or none. `idempotencyKey` is the pass's own key
(`plan:<entryId>:pass`): the same key again answers with the first answer and writes nothing. It changes the
row's state, so a stale `revision` conflicts.
PassPickBody.title: PassPickBody

PassResult.description:
Not now on a pick: the row left today's list (the company is kept everywhere, it is not a no-go), and the
next best company from the bench took its place, or none when the bench is empty.
PassResult.title: PassResult

PostingFlag.description: One field where the reader and the phrase rules disagree (or the reader could not say), with both quotes.
PostingFlag.title: PostingFlag

ProfileRole.description: An open engineering role at his level: what the profile's roles list shows.
ProfileRole.title: ProfileRole

ProfileValue.description:
One fact of a company's profile in the words the page shows. `text` is None when nothing is known (the page says
"Not known", never an error); `note` says how sure it is and where it comes from ("estimate, LinkedIn").
ProfileValue.title: ProfileValue

QueueOpening.description: The opening a pick names (top picks, 2026-10-26): the row's role, its level and age, and whether it is new.
QueueOpening.title: QueueOpening

QueueStanding.description:
Where a company stands (`outreach.plan.contact`): new, a wave in flight, asked before with no answer, or a
reply that holds it. `text` is the line the row shows.
QueueStanding.title: QueueStanding

ReplyRate.description: Of the emails first sent this month, how many have a reply (a cohort, so the rate is never above 1).
ReplyRate.title: ReplyRate

SaveSearchBody.description: His LinkedIn people search for the row's company, the address as he copied it from his browser.
SaveSearchBody.title: SaveSearchBody

SkipRowBody.description: Carry the row to tomorrow. It changes the row's state, so a stale `revision` conflicts.
SkipRowBody.title: SkipRowBody

UndoStepBody.description: Take back the newest step he logged (only the newest, so the steps left always make sense).
UndoStepBody.title: UndoStepBody

WatchDismissed.description: What a dismiss answers with: the id it was sent. (A write answers with JSON; an empty answer reads as broken.)
WatchDismissed.title: WatchDismissed
